summary: Satya Vrat Shastri (1930–2021) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied under Charu Deva Shastri, Shukdev Jha, and Siddheshwar Varma, attending University of the Punjab, Banaras Hindu University, and Punjabi University. He served at Delhi University (1970–1995).

Satyendra Nath Bose (1894–1974) studied at Hindu School, Presidency University, and University College of Science, Technology & Agriculture. He taught at Dhaka University (1921–1945), Calcutta University (1916; physics professor 1945–1956), and was Vice-chancellor of Visva-Bharati University (~1956–1958).

Sayadaw U Pandita (1921–2016) was a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. He studied under Nandasiri Sayadaw and Mahasi Sayadaw, taught meditation at Mahasi Sasana Yeiktha (from 1955), succeeded Mahasi Sayadaw (1982–1991), and served as abbot of Panditarama Meditation Center.

Sayadaw U Silananda (1927–2005) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Sayadaw U Pannavanta, Mahasi Sayadaw, and at University College, Colombo. He served as abbot at multiple monasteries, Spiritual Director of the Theravada Buddhist Society of America (1979–2005), and ITBMU Chancellor (1999).

Sayadaw U Thittila (1896–1997) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Sayadaw Ashin Adiccavamsa and at Visva-Bharati University (~1933–1934). He was a librarian at Adyar Library and The Buddhist Society (~1938) and taught at the University of Rangoon (1952).
Sayaka Sonoda is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. She completed her PhD at Toyo University under the supervision of Shinobu Yamaguchi.

Scott A. Mitchell is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. He earned his PhD at the Graduate Theological Union under Richard K. Payne (attested 2008) and served as a professor at the Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 2015).

Scott Pacey is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. After completing his doctorate at the Australian National University in 2011, he held posts at Hebrew University of Jerusalem and the University of Manchester (attested 2014).

Sean D. Gaffney works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at SOAS University of London, where he completed his PhD under Tadeusz Skorupski (attested 2003) and also studied under Philip T. Denwood, Renate Söhnen-Thieme, Alexander Piatigorsky, and David Seyfort Ruegg.
Sebastian Pole is an Indology scholar who studied at the East West College of Herbalism, the London College of Traditional Acupuncture and Oriental Medicine, and the College of Ayurveda.
See Mui Yian is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned a PhD at The University of Hong Kong under the supervision of K. L. Dhammajoti (attested 2010).

Seema Alavi (born 1961) is an Indology and history scholar. She earned her doctorate from the University of Cambridge, taught at the University of Delhi and Jawaharlal Nehru University, and held history professorships at Jamia Millia Islamia and Ashoka University (~2020).

Seigai Omura (1868–1927) was a scholar of archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He studied at Tokyo University of the Arts (~1889–1893) under Kanō Tomonobu, subsequently serving there as assistant professor (1896) and professor (1898).

Seiichi Mizuno (1905–1971) was a scholar in archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He studied at Kyoto University under Kosaku Hamada, later working at Kyoto University's Institute for Research in Humanities (1938, 1961) and as university professor (1949–1968).

Seiichi Yagi (born 1932) is a scholar of religious studies, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1951–1955) and held posts at Kanto Gakuin University, Tokyo Institute of Technology (~1968–1989), and Toin University of Yokohama.

Seiichiro Ono (1891–1986) studied at First Higher School and the University of Tokyo under Eiichi Makino, Daito Shimaji, Kanae Tada, and Jokan Chikazumi. He served as professor at the University of Tokyo (1922; 1938–1951) and Aichi Gakuin University (1957–1977).

Seiji Kimura (born 1957) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University (attested 1986). He later held posts at Komazawa University (attested 1990) and Komazawa Junior College (attested 1995).
Seiji Kumagai (born 1980) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at Kyoto University (~2005–2008) and became an associate professor there around 2013.
Seiji Nemoto (born 1949) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at Meiji University (~1968–1972) and was a professor at the University of Tsukuba (~2001–2015).
Seiji Tanaka (1897–1994) studied under Bruno Petzold and held academic posts at Aoyama Gakuin University (~1962–1974) and Asia University (~1974–1985).
